Class ChaosQuarkusBuildStep

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.quarkus.deployment.ChaosQuarkusBuildStep
public final class ChaosQuarkusBuildStep extends Object
Build-time processor that registers the chaos-agent extension with the Quarkus build graph.

This class lives in the deployment artifact — a separate jar from the runtime artifact — so that io.quarkus.deployment.* types never leak onto the application's runtime classpath. Quarkus discovers the class via the deployment-artifact: pointer declared in the runtime module's META-INF/quarkus-extension.yaml.

The work is intentionally split across two BuildStep methods:

  • feature() — a non-recording step that produces the FeatureBuildItem so the feature appears in the Quarkus startup banner. Must NOT be @Record — Quarkus forbids returning a build item other than void or a BytecodeRecorderObjectLoader from a recording step.
  • installChaosAgent(ChaosQuarkusRecorder) — a recording step whose sole responsibility is to emit the runtime-init call into the recorder bytecode. It returns void and performs no build-item production, satisfying the recording contract.

The two are separate methods because one method returning FeatureBuildItem while annotated @Record(RUNTIME_INIT) fails the build: the deployment engine would run it both for recording and for the build-item output.

    • producerBean

      public io.quarkus.arc.deployment.AdditionalBeanBuildItem producerBean()
      Registers ChaosArcProducer as a bean. The runtime jar carries no Jandex index and no beans.xml, so ArC would not discover the producer on its own. Unremovable because the bean is typically injected only into test classes, which ArC does not see as injection points.
      Returns:
      the additional-bean registration

    • chaosTestClassBeans

      public void chaosTestClassBeans(io.quarkus.deployment.builditem.CombinedIndexBuildItem index, io.quarkus.deployment.annotations.BuildProducer<io.quarkus.deployment.builditem.TestClassBeanBuildItem> testClassBeans)
      Makes every test class annotated with @QuarkusChaosTest a bean, and every concrete subclass of one (the annotation is inherited), as Quarkus does for a @QuarkusTest class, so its @Inject fields are injected. Quarkus finds a test class only by an @ExtendWith(QuarkusTestExtension.class) it sees in the indexed test classes; the one on @QuarkusChaosTest is in this extension's jar, which it does not index, so without this step a @QuarkusChaosTest class with an injected field cannot be instantiated.
      Parameters:
      index - the application's combined index, which holds the test classes in test mode
      testClassBeans - where the test classes are registered

    • installChaosAgent

      public void installChaosAgent(ChaosQuarkusRecorder recorder)
      Records the runtime-init call that installs the chaos agent before any application code runs.

      Void return and @Record(RUNTIME_INIT): the build step is a pure recorder with no build-item output. The generated bytecode calls ChaosQuarkusRecorder.installAgent() on the live recorder at application startup.

      Parameters:
      recorder - the build-time recorder proxy; method calls on it are recorded as bytecode
